To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhibitory action on AH neurons of adenosine (a purine) in the myenteric pike of the small intestine of the guinea pig is due to suppression of adenylatecyclase activity and consequent reduction in intracellular levels of cyclic AMP (cAMP).
adenosine inhibits the electrical activity of myenteric neurons by reducing the levels of cyclic AMP in the cell.
Adenosine, a purinergic agonist, hyperpolarizes and decreases the excitability of AH‐type myenteric neurone in the guinea‐pigs intestine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of purines and purinergic receptors in the enteric nervous system of the guinea pig.
the effects of adenosine, a purine nucleoside, on the electrophysiological behaviour of myenterc neurones in the guinea-pig ileum.
the role of purine‐mediated signalling in the small intestinal enteric nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenosine is an inhibitor of myenteric AH/type 2 neurones in guinea‐pigs.
the inhibitory action is a result of suppression of adenylate‐cyclase‐mediated cyclic AMP formation.
the inhibitory actions of adenosines are mediated by a purinergic receptor‐adenylate cyclase pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adenosine acts on the AH/type 2 cells by inhibiting adenylate cyclases, whereas ATP and ADP are likely to act by activating P2X‐purinoreceptors.

the inhibitory action on the electrical activity of AH/type 2 neurones is mediated by adenosine acting on A1 receptors, which in turn suppresses the activity of adenyl cyclase, and thereby intracellular levels of cyclic AMP.
adenosine acts on AH/type 2 neurones by inhibiting adenylate cyclases and thereby suppressing the excitatory actions mediated by cyclic AMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibitory effects of adenosine are due to a direct effect on the myenteric neurone, and not due to a reduction of excitatory neurotransmitter release.
adenosine is an effective inhibitor of the excitatory actions mediated by cyclic AMP in the myenteric plicuses of the small intestine of the guinea pig.
we have shown that adenosine, acting at P1 receptors, can inhibit enteric neurons through a mechanism that does not involve the cyclic AMP pathway.
